summary: Builtin chainLoadGate + engine last-good fallback so a broken self-edited chain.ts can't crash a long-running loop, per §3

edit.description: Add chainLoadGate: on a tick that touched .flume/chain.ts, validate it loads and default-exports a valid Chain (same checks diskChainLoader makes).
Export chainLoadGate (additive to v0.1 §2 builtin-gate list).
Engine fallback: per-tick resolution throws with no gate caught → retain last-good chain module, log a loud error, continue the loop.
chainLoadGate: valid post-tick chain passes; broken chain fails → producing tick reverts.
Resolution failure, no gate declared → last-good retained, error logged, loop() does not throw.

tests.asserts: valid post-tick chain.ts passes chainLoadGate; syntactically-broken chain.ts fails → producing tick reverted
resolution failure with no gate → engine retains last-good chain, logs error, loop() does not throw (§3 acceptance)

acceptance: Broken chain.ts with chainLoadGate declared → tick reverted, chain restored, loop continues; resolution failure w/o gate → last-good retained, error logged, no throw
notes: Both layers required (§3). PER-TICK-CHAIN-RELOAD moved load+validate into diskChainLoader (Dispatcher.ts:82) — gate mirrors those checks against the post-tick file, not the memoized module (loadChain no longer exists). Dogfood .flume/chain.ts does NOT declare chainLoadGate (no flume-on-flume phase writes chain.ts) — engine fallback is its net. No .flume/chain.ts edit.

summary: Serialize .git/worktrees/-mutating ops: setup Promise.all (Dispatcher.ts:366) + teardown (:468) → sequential for…await; keep agent fanout (:393) parallel

edit.description: createWorktree loop (:366) and teardown loop (:468) → sequential for…await; per-entry agent Promise.all (:393) stays parallel.
Stale-slug-seeded N≥2 wave: all worktrees created + entries shipped; teardown leaves git worktree list clean; fanout-parallelism assertion stays green.

tests.asserts: stale-slug N≥2 wave completes (no add fails on sibling remove); teardown leaves clean git worktree list; existing fanout-parallelism assertion stays green (§4 acceptance)

acceptance: Stale-slug N≥2 wave completes with all worktrees created + entries shipped; teardown leaves git worktree list clean; existing fanout-parallelism assertion green
notes: Cites re-anchored to post-PER-TICK-CHAIN-RELOAD Dispatcher.ts (diskChainLoader added ~140 lines): setup :366, agent fanout :393, teardown :468 (spec §4 says :257/:284/:353 — pre-reload). Internal git.ts/Dispatcher.ts (not v0.1 §2) → CHANGELOG ### Fixed, non-breaking. blockedBy is ordering-only; linearizes so RELEASE-0.2.0 gates on one tag. All v0.2 entries touch src/Dispatcher.ts → fanout partitioner serializes them regardless.

summary: Cut 0.2.0: package.json version → 0.2.0; CHANGELOG ## [0.2.0] with ### Breaking / ### Added / ### Fixed per §5

edit.description: Add ## [0.2.0]: ### Breaking (DispatcherOptions removed chain; resolution per-tick from configDir), ### Added (chainLoadGate, per-tick chain re-resolution), ### Fixed (worktree create/teardown race serialization).

acceptance: package.json is 0.2.0; CHANGELOG has ## [0.2.0] with the three subsections; pnpm build clean; v0.1 §8 consumer-install smoke + attw green in CI
notes: Single consolidated [0.2.0] section avoids 3-way CHANGELOG cherry-pick conflicts → a release-cut entry blockedBy the last functional entry. npm publish + git tag are human release-ceremony (cf. open-questions tag lane), out of build's scope. CONTINGENT: `### Added (per-tick chain re-resolution)` wording depends on OQ '§2 in-process reload' — if disposition (d), soften to 're-resolution across loop-process boundaries'; do not ship an over-claiming CHANGELOG.
